events.title: The fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.shortBlurb: The last emperor in the West was deposed, and the Church became the enduring institution of a collapsing world…
body: In August 476 the barbarian soldiers of Italy — Heruli, Rugii, and Sciri among them — rose under their commander Odoacer to claim the lands promised them, and put the general Orestes to death at Piacenza. On 4 September Odoacer entered Ravenna and compelled Orestes' young son, the emperor Romulus, mockingly styled Augustulus, 'little Augustus,' to lay down the purple.

Sparing the boy with a pension and a villa in Campania, Odoacer sent the imperial insignia to the Emperor Zeno at Constantinople and ruled Italy as king under the East's nominal overlordship. No emperor reigned again in the West: Julius Nepos, the last claimant recognized by Constantinople, held out in Dalmatia only until 480. Later ages fixed on this quiet abdication as the fall of the Western Roman Empire.

The change was less a single blow than the last step of a long dissolution. As civil authority failed, the Catholic Church remained the one institution spanning the old empire: her bishops kept order in the cities, her monasteries guarded learning, and the see of Rome became the fixed point of the West — the vision Augustine, dead a generation before at besieged Hippo, had framed in his City of God.
